subject: Launch readiness: TTFT + streaming handshake and capacity qualification
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@edgescale.com>, Maya Roy <maya.roy@edgescale.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Launch readiness: TTFT + streaming handshake and capacity qual

Thanks for the call earlier — quick recap and action items geared toward the pilot scoping and TTFT SLOs.

Summary (what we heard):
- Primary goal: <200 ms TTFT for the interactive chat flow at 95th percentile during steady load; target 150 ms for initial pilot if possible.
- Preferred streaming: SSE initially (client stack already supports EventSource), websocket fallback acceptable for certain clients.
- Chunk cadence: clients expect first meaningful chunk within 50–150 ms of start of emission, then steady chunks no slower than 300–500 ms under normal token rates.
- Concurrency: baseline 100 concurrent active sessions, peak bursts up to 500 concurrent; expected sustained throughput ~40 reqs/s with median conversation length ~120 tokens.

Immediate asks for EdgeScale (please confirm):
1) Sample traffic profile: payload sizes, avg tokens per request, concurrent users during peak. (Sanjay — you said you'd share CSV.)
2) Success metrics: confirm TTFT p95 target (we proposed 150 ms for pilot) and acceptable degrade bands.
3) Pilot window: propose week of July 12 for a 2-week pilot (dev -> integration -> production-to-staging traffic).

Redwood action items:
- Ben/Karthik: propose pilot config (dedicated pool or burst policy), initial autoscaling params, and fallback policy to smaller model for overload.
- I'll share a draft SoW and a latency matrix template attachment.

Attachments: edgescale_latency_matrix.xlsx (template), payload_samples.jsonl (example shapes).

Thanks — will set up a 30-minute pilot kickoff once we have traffic CSV.

— Olga
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@edgescale.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Roy <maya.roy@edgescale.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 16:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Launch readiness: TTFT + streaming handshake and capacity qual

Thanks, Olga — appreciate the crisp recap.

Confirming a few things from our side:
- We can commit to providing the traffic CSV by Monday (incl. per-region splits and token histograms).
- For the pilot we are comfortable with a 150–200 ms p95 TTFT target; if you think 150 is achievable for pilot that would be great.
- SSE is preferred. We'll need websocket for mobile web where EventSource isn't reliable.
- Typical request payloads: 800–1,200 bytes; median returned tokens ~90, 95th around 260. Peak concurrent active sessions usually top at 420 for marketing spikes.

We can do the pilot week of July 12. We'll need an integration checklist (network allowlist, authentication, and a short test harness) — send us that.

Sanjay
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@edgescale.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Launch readiness: TTFT + streaming handshake and capacity qual

Couple quick notes for the pilot config:
- Suggest starting on Redwood Dedicated with a small reserved pool (2 GPUs) + burst capacity. That keeps BTU low and gives predictable p95.
- Autoscale policy: target CPU/GPU utilization 60–70% with burst headroom for 1.5x expected peak; helps keep chunk cadence consistent.
- Chunking/pacing: we can prime the first 20–30 tokens to ensure the first chunk arrives quickly (reduces TTFT variance). We'll instrument client-side latency markers.
- Fallbacks: define a model-variant fallback path if latency spikes >250 ms for more than 2 minutes.

I'll put together the pilot config doc and an ops runbook. Karthik — will need your help validating the SSE handshake and heartbeat interval (we usually default to 15s heartbeat for proxies).

-Ben
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@edgescale.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Launch readiness: TTFT + streaming handshake and capacity qual

Thanks — adding a few technical clarifications and open questions for the kickoff:
- Network: we need NAT/egress IPs for allowlisting; Sanjay, please confirm your egress ranges or whether you prefer a VPN.
- Client heartbeat: 15s default is fine; we'll recommend 8s for mobile clients behind flaky networks.
- Chunk cadence: agree on priming 20–30 tokens; we'll aim for first-chunk emission <120 ms in lab for the pilot model. Real-world p95 will vary.
- KV cache and warm starts: if EdgeScale can warm the model with a small burst of representative sessions before peak, TTFT improves substantially.
- Measurement: we'll instrument three markers — client connect, first-chunk-received, final-token — and share dashboards.

I'll attach a short checklist for the integration to this thread and update the SoW.

— Karthik
